summary:
**ASCLEPIUS: Project Summary**

**Overview**
ASCLEPIUS is an autonomous onboard health monitoring system for astronauts on long-duration missions. It guarantees 90 days of operational autonomy during communication blackouts with Earth.

**Architecture & Tech**
Built as a zero-dependency Progressive Web App (PWA) in a single HTML file, it runs locally. It uses an offline analytics engine combining rule-based logic and EWMA models for real-time anomaly detection. Data is secured via AES-256-GCM encryption and FNV-1a integrity hashing.

**Key Capabilities**

* Monitors crew vitals including HR, SpO₂, blood pressure, HRV, sleep, and mood.


* Tracks cabin environment telemetry like CO₂, O₂, radiation, and pressure.


* Provides offline step-by-step guidance for emergencies like radiation storms or hypoxia.


* Manages personalized NASA/ESA countermeasure protocols.


* Features a priority transmission queue, medical data exports (FHIR, CSV, JSON), role-based access, and a simulation training mode.
details:
Core Function: "ASCLEPIUS" is an autonomous onboard health monitoring and management system designed for astronauts on long-duration space missions.

How it works: It operates as a 24/7 Progressive Web App (PWA) with a single-file architecture that functions entirely offline. It continuously tracks physiological vitals (heart rate, SpO₂, blood pressure, temperature, HRV, bone density, sleep, mood) and cabin environmental telemetry (CO₂, O₂, radiation, pressure).

Intelligence & Comms: It utilizes an offline analytics engine combining rule-based logic and Exponentially Weighted Moving Average (EWMA) models to detect anomalies. It guides crews through step-by-step emergency protocols, manages personalized countermeasure tasks (NASA/ESA guidelines), and queues critical reports for transmission back to Earth via a priority queue when a communication link becomes available.

What benefits does it have?

  • 90-Day Absolute Autonomy: Fully operational without requiring a real-time connection to Earth, making it ideal for deep space exploration or total communication blackouts.
  • Real-Time Offline Anomaly Detection: Instantly identifies critical deviations and health hazards locally without cloud processing dependency.
  • Robust Data Security: Secures all stored logs and metrics locally using AES-256-GCM encryption (via PBKDF2 key derivation) and cryptographic data integrity hashing (FNV-1a).
  • Comprehensive Care Matrix: Combines wearable sensor feeds, onboard medical instruments (ultrasound metadata, blood analyzers), environmental monitoring, and dedicated risk assessment models (radiation, decompression sickness, orthostatic intolerance, psychological strain).

What is the intended impact of the project?

  • Ensuring Crew Survivability & Readiness: To safeguard the health, safety, and operational performance of astronauts during extended deep-space missions (such as Mars transit or long orbital stays).
  • Mitigating Space Hazards: Proactively preventing or managing microgravity-induced degradation (bone/muscle loss), radiation exposure, hypoxia, and acute psychological distress without relying heavily on ground control oversight.

What tools, coding languages, hardware, or software did you use to develop your project?

  • Languages & Core Technologies: HTML5, CSS3, and Vanilla JavaScript (ES6+) built into a single, self-contained file with zero external dependencies.
    • Web Audio API (for customized alert and confirmation sounds).
    • Web Crypto API (for AES-256-GCM vault encryption).
    • Speech Recognition API (for voice-to-text note input).
    • Custom SVG canvas rendering for real-time ECG waveforms and trend charts.
  • Data & Standards: Local database persistence via localStorage, supporting standard medical/data export bundles including HL7 FHIR, CSV, and JSON formats.
  • Hardware Simulated/Supported: Wearable health patches/straps (HR, ECG, SpO₂, temperature, EEG, accelerometers) and onboard medical instruments (blood analyzers, ultrasound devices, microgravity mass scales, blood pressure monitors, dynamometers).

How is your project creative?

  • Single-File Zero-Dependency Architecture: The entire complex medical dashboard, local database engine, dynamic SVG charting library, cryptographic vault, and emergency protocol wizard are packaged into a single HTML file, ensuring maximum portability and fail-safe deployment in space hardware.
  • Built-in Training & Simulation Mode: Features a real-time synthetic data engine with toggleable modeled deviations and emergency scenarios (such as radiation storms, cardiac events, or decompression sickness) to test system resilience and response algorithms instantly.
  • Self-Sustaining Offline UX: Delivers a smooth, native-like application experience complete with multi-language support (Ukrainian/English), high-contrast accessibility modes, and interactive drag-and-drop protocol task management without needing an internet connection.

What factors did your team consider?

  • Communication Latency & Blackouts: Designed around deep-space realities where signal delay or total loss of link is common, implementing a strict 90-day autonomy guarantee and a priority-based transmission queue.
  • Space-Specific Medical Risks: Addressed unique physiological hazards of spaceflight, including fluid shifts, bone density depletion, muscle atrophy, hypercapnia (high CO₂), solar radiation spikes, and decompression sickness (DCS).
  • Security & Role-Based Access: Considered data privacy and permissions by establishing strict boundaries between roles (Astronaut viewing/editing personal profile vs. Mission Physician viewing all crew data vs. Ground Control read-only access).
  • Human Factors & Astronaut Ergonomics: Minimized cognitive load during high-stress scenarios through clear visual risk indicators, audio cues, font scaling, and step-by-step emergency wizards.
